briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan's tax squeeze meets a national psychedelic breakthrough
briefs.top: The state's new 24% wholesale tax is already forcing closures across metro Detroit — even as the first FDA-approved psilocybin therapy moves within reach nationally. Here's what matters, close to home and coast to coast.

local.text: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax is biting: the Senate Fiscal Agency projects a 14.4% sales drop — $400–450M wiped from the market this year.
Ann Arbor's C3 Industries is closing its 35,000 sq ft Webberville grow and cutting 62 jobs — the CEO says the model isn't sustainable under the new tax.
The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association (400+ businesses) is fighting to strike the 24% tax as unconstitutional — a Court of Claims judge is letting the suit proceed.
Five metro cities — Ann Arbor, Detroit, Ferndale, Hazel Park & Ypsilanti — now deprioritize psychedelic enforcement. Note: that's not legalization.
Statewide, SB 631 — the Michigan Psychedelics & Mental Health Act — is still pending; psilocybin remains Schedule I under state law.
Bright spot: Michigan drinkers are trading beer for THC — cannabis beverages are the fastest-shifting category heading into the tax era.

national.text: Cannabis rescheduling is at the one-yard line: final post-hearing briefs were filed Aug 17, with a Schedule III move on an expedited track since April.
The federal hemp-THC ban got a reprieve — a stopgap pushed the effective date from Nov 12 to Dec 11; without a fix, ~95% of hemp-derived products go unlawful.
Psilocybin is close to history: Compass Pathways' COMP360 filing is on track for Q4, teeing up the first FDA-approved psychedelic therapy by late 2026 or early 2027.
Washington is pushing: a Trump executive order plus FDA 'priority vouchers' to Compass, Usona & Transcend can compress review from ~12 months to 1–2.
The FDA finalized its psychedelic clinical-trial guidance — the clearest regulatory roadmap this class has ever had, fixing the trial 'unblinding' problem.
Mark your calendar: the FDA holds a public hearing on the therapeutic use of psychedelics on Sept 14.
